one_month_reasoning: AMD's own Q3 print is expected around 2026-11-03 (unconfirmed, based on last year's timing), i.e. just AFTER the 2026-10-30 window, so the stock's own earnings are not in the window. Inside the window: hyperscaler Q3 reports and capex guides (Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon typically the last week of October) and peer semis prints; these move AI-GPU names but direction is unknown. The stock ran ~32% in 15 sessions into late September (to $630 on Sep 25) and has pulled back to $604; short-horizon reversal after a sharp run vs. momentum roughly cancel, with a slight tilt toward mean reversion given valuation-driven downgrades and CEO 10b5-1 sales. Pre-earnings run-ups are common for AMD. Net: near-symmetric lognormal centred ~$600 (tiny negative drift) with sigma ~19% (72% annual vol / 3.5, trimmed slightly because the earnings event itself falls outside).

fair_value.method: Blend of (a) P/E on FY2028 EPS ~$21 x 28x less ~5% expected warrant dilution = ~$560 (60%) and (b) P/E on skeptic-haircut FY2027 EPS $14 x 38x = ~$532 (40%); blended ~$550, about 9% below spot.

bull.story: Helios ships on time, OpenAI/Meta/Oracle/Anthropic deployments scale, data center GPU revenue compounds >80%, FY28 EPS path toward $28+, market keeps a 30-35x forward multiple; warrant dilution is accepted as cheap customer acquisition.

thesis_break_reason: A close below ~$400 (-34%) would most likely mean a fundamental event rather than volatility: a confirmed Helios/MI450 volume slip into late 2027, a hyperscaler capex cut, or a guide-down that pulls FY27 EPS toward ~$11. At that price the stock would sit ~25x the consensus FY28 path, so only a lower earnings path explains it.

reasoning: Starting facts: $604 close, ~$985B market cap on 1.632B shares, trailing P/E ~200x, ~80-90x 2026 EPS ($7-7.6), ~39x consensus 2027 EPS ($15.58), up 281% in a year. Fundamentals are strong and not in dispute: Q2 revenue +50% to $11.5B, data center +107%, Q3 guide $13B (+41%), 56% non-GAAP GM, investment-grade balance sheet with essentially net-neutral cash after a $4.75B August bond deal at 4.6-5.5% (no credit stress). The skeptic case therefore rests not on solvency or accounting but on (1) valuation: at 39x NTM+1 EPS the stock already discounts the 2027 consensus; to rise it needs estimates to keep climbing; (2) execution: credible trade reporting of Helios rack ramp problems and a mass-production slip into 2027, which AMD denies; (3) the warrant model: 320M $0.01 warrants (19.6% dilution) granted to OpenAI and Meta; critics (RightClick Research, Enertuition, SA 'circular financing') argue it signals weak organic demand and transfers wealth; SemiAnalysis shows the warrants push customers' effective GPU cost toward zero at $600-700 share prices, which also means AMD's reported margins overstate economic margins; (4) CEO 10b5-1 sales ($17M Mar, $58M Jun, $48M Sep) - routine, weak signal; (5) no sell ratings among 55 analysts, and the average target ($568-619) is at or below spot, so sell-side offers little upside. No short-seller report or securities class action found. Weighing honestly: consensus is not obviously wrong on earnings, but the price embeds it. Fair value ~$550 (-9%). Distribution: lognormal median ~$570 with sigma ~0.52 (below the 72% realized vol, which was inflated by a one-way 280% run, but above the 25-35% large-cap base rate), fat left tail added for an AI-capex bust. Scenario mean ~$597, i.e. flat vs spot. P(>= spot) ~45%. Research limits: Twelve Data estimates/insider endpoints unavailable on plan; no prediction markets or X posts checked; the 2027 consensus figure comes from aggregators with inconsistent values ($11-15.6).
